chapter: Rhythm Club memories and playing technique
title: Forgotten Harlem fiddlers, banjoists and drummers

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Oh yeah. But there used to be a good fiddle player around then by the name of Bobby Hargraves. Used to be another banjo player around then. Later on he switched over to guitar. Seminole. Have you ever heard that name before?
Yeah, Seminole. Great banjo player. Have you ever heard the name of Banjo Berney?
Well Banjo Berney, he was another great banjo player. Of course you've heard of Juice Wilson?

Yeah, Juice Wilson, fiddle, very good. See this is going way back there you know, and these are guys that were around the Band Box and the Rhythm Club. But they never did get well known, but they could play, you know, like Seminole, Juice Wilson, they could really play.
There are I guess a lot of guys who just got lost in the shuffle there.
That's right, that's right, see and just--
During the Depression I suppose they couldn't make a living and got into something else.
See a lot of drummers around there, there were a lot of good drummers around there. Steve Wright.
Zeno Lawrence. Willy Lynch. Clubfoot Jenkins. All these are drummers.
That's a name for a drummer.
Yup, Cripple Smitty, good drummers. Tommy Benford, of course he's still playing.
I heard him a couple of years ago, he sounds great.

Oh yeah, yeah, got a good beat. Yeah, Tommy Bedford. But there were quite a few names around there then got lost in the shuffle you know. Piano player Price Jones and Dick Edwards, they were good pianists. Used to go on those little gigs with them sometime, play in those house parties. And--
